subject: Sunday Setlist — October 18: half the set is in 6/8
intro: You got the setlist Tuesday. Here's what to do with it by Sunday. Six songs the charts say you're most likely to play on October 18: four that have sat in the CCLI top 20 all year, plus two climbing right now — both of them gratitude songs, which is a ramp that starts about now and runs through November. One thing worth knowing before you build: three of the six are in 6/8, where a dotted-eighth delay quietly ruins everything. It all runs off one AC30-style base (Essex A30 on Helix), a Klon-style boost always on, one delay block and one plate. Build it once, then change two numbers per song.

songs.title: What a Beautiful Name
songs.tone: 68 BPM in D — dotted-eighth at 662 ms, two repeats, mix around 22%. Verses sit on snapshot 1 (Clean) with the boost already on; the title-line lift is snapshot 5 (Clean Ambi) with the plate up, not more gain. Save snapshot 3 (Drive+) for the final chorus — the song peaks once, and if you spend it in verse 2 you have nowhere left to go.

links.label: Full recipe: Nigel Hendroff's What a Beautiful Name tone
What a Beautiful Name on Helix

songs.title: Gratitude
songs.tone: 78 BPM in B, and it's 6/8 — so kill the dotted eighth. At 45000÷78 it lands on 577 ms and fights the compound-meter grouping until the part smears; use the straight eighth instead, 30000÷78 = 385 ms, with mix back at 12%. Snapshot 1 (Clean) carries the verses on the AC30's bloom alone, and the stripped bridge wants you off the strings entirely.

links.label: Why the dotted eighth breaks in 6/8

songs.title: Trust In God
songs.tone: Charted at 148 BPM in C and felt in 6/8, which gives you two usable eighth-note times: 203 ms against the driving subdivision, 405 ms against the half-time 74 feel. Pick per section — 203 ms on snapshot 2 (Drive) for the choruses, 405 ms on snapshot 5 (Clean Ambi) for the verses. Same preset, one delay-time change, and the part stops arguing with the drummer.

links.label: Elevation Worship guitar tone on Helix

songs.title: Firm Foundation (He Won't)
songs.tone: The studio cut is 75 BPM in Db and live versions run it at 150 — either way it's 6/8, so straight eighths again: 200 ms at the fast count, 400 ms at the slow one. The trap here is reverb, not delay — a long plate under a 150 BPM 6/8 turns the chorus to mush, so pull decay back to 1.6 s and predelay to 20 ms. Snapshot 2 (Drive) through the verses, snapshot 6 (Ambi Drive) once the room is singing.

links.label: Worship guitar tone on Helix (the base preset)
When reverb tails collide with the tempo

songs.title: God I'm Just Grateful
songs.tone: 72 BPM in D and properly 4/4, so you finally get a clean dotted eighth: 625 ms, three repeats, mix 25%. This is a volume-pedal song — snapshot 5 (Clean Ambi), heel down, swell into each chord change with no pick attack at all. Snapshot 4 (Lead) only for the turnaround.

songs.title: In The Presence Of The King
songs.tone: 73 BPM in G — dotted eighth at 616 ms, two repeats, mix 20%. New enough that most rooms are still learning it, so keep the build obvious: snapshot 1 (Clean) through the verses, snapshot 3 (Drive+) from the chorus, boost on the whole way. If it's fighting the keys, that's 2 dB out at 2.5 kHz, not a different amp.

links.label: Single-coil vs humbucker for ambient worship

outro: Six songs, one preset, two numbers that change. The 6/8 thing is the whole lesson this week: if a song feels like it's counted in three, the dotted eighth is working against you and the straight eighth is the fix. Everything else lives at faderandknob.com/guides/worship-guitar, and there's a Worship Set Pack if you'd rather load the presets than build them. Now the part I actually want: hit reply with your setlist for Sunday. I read every one, and the songs that keep showing up are the ones that get recipes next.
